2.text: Gradually he approaches so close to the seal as to be able to play the harpoon.

3.text: These two methods are quite similar to those of the American Eskimo.¹

4.text: Seals are also killed in the spring on the edges of the ice-cracks, where

5.text: they like to sleep at noontime. Before the breaking-up of the ice, wherever

6.text: small streams of fresh water run into the sea along an ice-crack, seals gather

7.text: around their outlet to bask in the sunshine. A sealer will tie into a rough

8.text: bundle some scraps of old skin and send it downstream. It will float down

9.text: unobserved, but, on coming to one of the small whirlpools which form in the

10.text: crack, it will pop out suddenly and frighten away the seals lying around, so

11.text: that they can easily be overtaken on the ice. Seals sleeping on the ice, when

12.text: suddenly frightened, will often lose their holes and crawl away in the wrong

13.text: direction. Then they can easily be overtaken, especially the younger ones.

14.text: Perhaps this accounts for the method of hunting of the Netchillirmiut, reported

15.text: by J. Ross,² where a party of hunters slowly approach the sleeping seal, then

16.text: those in front shout as loudly as they can, and the others run up to the seal

17.text: and spear it. A basking seal sometimes sleeps so soundly that it may be

18.text: caught by a fast-running dog-team before it wakes up. At other times it

19.text: will lose its hole altogether, and will be found crawling helplessly on the ice.

20.text: The natives say that this is because the seal wants to take a walk on the

21.text: ice from one to another of its holes, but loses its way.

22.text: In some places large numbers of seals are killed while trying to go over

23.text: a narrow strip of land between the sea and the inner bay. Occasionally the

24.text: seals make quite long trips overland. Thus they ascend the largest rivers,

25.text: like the Kolyma and the Anadyr, for more than a hundred miles. During

26.text: my stay in the Kolyma country a seal was even caught on the middle course

27.text: of the Dry Anui, about two hundred miles from the mouth of the Kolyma.

28.text: Trustworthy people relate that the seals which ascend the Anadyr after the

29.text: salmon-shoals often turn into its affluents, the Kanchalan and Big Rivers.

30.text: If belated for return by river, on account of low water or early frosts, they

31.text: start on a quite wonderful overland journey on impracticable roads among

32.text: the hills. I was shown the skin of a rough-seal killed on such a journey in

34.text: All through the winter, wherever the open water is not far from the

35.text: shore, the natives go sealing and walrusing at the edge of the land-ice. The

36.text: animals are shot in the water or on the drifting ice. Then, if feasible, they

37.text: are secured by means of a special implement (Fig. 37), which is made of

38.text: wood, is round and somewhat spindle-shaped, and has several iron hooks, and

39.text: a long stout line at the bottom. It is flung at the passing body, and, if the
